claim_verdicts.evidence: stage-1 scripts/dev-secrets.sh:16-23 is exactly the block quoted: if ! grep -q '^JWT_SIGNING_KEY=' .env ... echo "JWT_SIGNING_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 48)" >> .env. Live lab: the value after JWT_SIGNING_KEY= in .env is 64 characters (counted with wc -c, value not printed) = base64 of 48 bytes.

Ledger text now matches the code: Program.cs:23-24 `builder.Configuration["Jwt:SigningKey"] ?? throw new InvalidOperationException(...)` fires only on null; r1 live run with JWT_SIGNING_KEY= showed the container Up and requests failing with IDX10703. IssuerSigningKey = new SymmetricSecurityKey(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(signingKey)) at :38; JwtTokenService.cs:15-16 HmacSha256 on the same setting. Lesson wording "throws at startup if the setting is missing altogether" is accurate.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Program.cs:23 copies the value into the local `signingKey` before builder.Build(), and TokenValidationParameters is built from that local, so no reload can reach it. docker-compose.yml:92 sets it as an environment variable of the container. r1 live run: the key changed only when the container was recreated. Lesson wording "copies the key once, at startup, from an environment variable" matches.

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 8725 sec. 2.2: "Some applications use a keyed Message Authentication Code (MAC) algorithm, such as 'HS256', to sign tokens but supply a weak symmetric key with insufficient entropy (such as a human-memorable password). Such keys are vulnerable to offline brute-force or dictionary attacks once an attacker gets hold of such a token." Forgery by any key holder: Program.cs validates only by recomputing with IssuerSigningKey (plus iss/aud/exp, all readable from a real token); no token store exists in stage-1.
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725 sec. 2.2; rfc7518 sec. 3.2; stage-1 Program.cs:22-41

claim_verdicts.evidence: Live run: login -> token; POST /api/v1/orders -> 201. After JWT_SIGNING_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 48) docker compose up -d api: 502 for ~3 s, then 401 with the same token. After docker compose up -d api: 502 for ~3 s, then 201 (order 35, status new) with the same token. Token lifetime is 8 h (JwtTokenService.cs:28 AddHours(8)), so the restore works only within that window.

Docker docs: "when the same variable is declared by multiple sources, precedence applies: 1. Variables from your shell environment 2. ... --env-file 3. ... .env file". Live output: "Container donhang-api Recreate / Recreated / Starting / Started" for both commands; after the restore the container's key hash equals the .env key hash. App: create_order_screen.dart sets 'Failed: $e' and api_client.dart:55 throws Exception('failed to create order (${response.statusCode})'), so a 401 renders "Failed: Exception: failed to create order (401)".

Follows from claim 4 and the code: OrdersController identity comes from the token's sub, so a forged sub acts as any customer; nothing in Program.cs depends on where the request comes from. RFC 8725 sec. 3.5: "Human-memorizable passwords MUST NOT be directly used as the key to a keyed-MAC algorithm such as 'HS256'."
git show stage-1:.gitignore -> line 1 `.env`. git show stage-1:docker-compose.yml -> line 92 `Jwt__SigningKey: "${JWT_SIGNING_KEY}"` under service api (line 82).

r1 live runs on stage-1: JWT_SIGNING_KEY=donhang -> login fails, API log "IDX10653: The encryption algorithm 'HS256' requires a key size of at least '128' bits"; after each docker compose up -d api, POST /api/v1/orders via Caddy returned 502 for ~3 s. Lesson says "about ten seconds" plus a retry-on-502 note: consistent. Note: the HS256/128-bit half is no longer used by the lesson or q2 after r1 fixes.

stage-1 Caddyfile: `handle /api/v1/* { reverse_proxy api:8080 }` on :8080 and donhang.local:8443, no auth/header-matching directive on that route; api_client.dart:11-12 baseUrl http://localhost:8080/api/v1 (Caddy). r1 live run: the 401 vs 201 via Caddy depended only on the API key. Bash run: `X=probe sh -c 'echo inside=$X'; echo after=${X:-unset}` -> inside=probe, after=unset.

issues.text: Unlisted claims added in r1 edits: (a) section 5, the `__` -> `:` mapping for environment variable names (a syntax rule of the ASP.NET Core configuration); (b) section 7 answer, the 8-hour token lifetime ("still within its eight hours"). Both are true: aspnetcore configuration docs: "A double underscore (`__`) is supported by all platforms and is automatically converted into a colon (`:`) when the configuration is read by the app"; JwtTokenService.cs:28 `expires: DateTime.UtcNow.AddHours(8)`.
issues.quote: the double underscore in a variable name stands for the `:` in a settings name, so the API sees it as `Jwt:SigningKey`
issues.fix: Leave the text. Add two claims: n=11 kind syntax, version_key aspnetcore, section 5, text "In environment variable names, __ is read as the : of a configuration key", source_hint refs/aspnetcore-docs/aspnetcore/fundamentals/configuration/index.md:276; n=12 kind fact, section 7, text "Tokens expire 8 hours after issue", source_hint stage-1 DonHang.Api/JwtTokenService.cs:28.
